title: Review: Using the Earth's resources and obtaining potable water; Life cycle assessment and recycling
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.10.1-c23, 4.10.1-c15, 4.10.1-c16, 4.10.2-c09. Clues: 4.10.1-c23 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.10.1-c15 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.10.1-c16 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.10.2-c09 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.10.1-q18, 4.10.2-q07, 4.10.2-q22, 4.10.1-q19, 4.10.2-q08, 4.10.2-q23, 4.10.1-q20, 4.10.2-q09, 4.10.2-q24, 4.10.1-q21, 4.10.2-q10, 4.10.1-q22.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Sedimentation
items.clue: Allowing sewage to stand so that solids settle out as sewage sludge, leaving liquid effluent above them.

items.label: Distillation
items.clue: Boiling water and condensing the vapour, so that the water separates from the dissolved solids, which stay behind.

items.label: Reverse osmosis
items.clue: A desalination process that forces salty water through a membrane which holds back the dissolved ions and lets water through.

items.label: Selective or abbreviated LCA
items.clue: A shortened life cycle assessment that considers only some stages, or only some impacts, of a product rather than the whole life cycle.

questions.stem: Which two methods of desalination does the specification name?

options.text: Filtering through sand, then sterilising it with chlorine
Distillation, or a membrane process like reverse osmosis
Crystallisation of the salt, followed by sedimentation
Anaerobic digestion followed by aerobic treatment

questions.explanation: The specification names distillation and processes that use membranes such as reverse osmosis.

questions.stem: A plastic garden chair is collected and buried in landfill at the end of its life. Which statement about the disposal stage of its LCA is correct?

options.text: Nothing is counted, because a chair sent to landfill is not processed
The transport of the chair and the burying of it are counted
Only the burying counts, since the lorry journey is a separate stage
Only the land the chair takes up in the landfill is counted

questions.explanation: Disposal includes collection and transport as well as the landfill itself, since transport is counted at each stage.

options.text: They are reused directly without any melting or processing
They are melted and then recast or reformed into products
They are melted only when every metal has been separated
They are crushed to powder and pressed into new shapes

questions.explanation: This is the method given in the specification for recycling metals.

questions.stem: The UK has plentiful rain. Why is desalination not used to supply most of its potable water?

options.text: Because sea water contains no dissolved salts in the UK
Because membranes cannot remove salt from sea water
Because desalination requires large amounts of energy
Because desalination is cheap but produces too little water

questions.explanation: The specification states desalination requires large amounts of energy, and rain supplies the UK with fresh water.

questions.stem: Which of these can be quantified fairly easily in a life cycle assessment?

options.text: The harm a pollutant does to a nearby river
How strongly local people object to the works
The mass of water used to make the item
The worth of the wildlife lost near a mine

questions.explanation: Use of water is named in the specification as something that can be quantified fairly easily.

questions.stem: At a steelworks, some scrap steel is added to the molten iron that comes from a blast furnace. Why is this done?

options.text: It acts as a fuel in the furnace, so less coke has to be burned
It removes the need to use any iron ore at the works at all
It separates unwanted metals out of the molten iron
It cuts the amount of iron that must be extracted from ore

questions.explanation: This is the reason given in the specification: less iron then has to be extracted from iron ore.

questions.stem: How does the treatment of salty water differ from the treatment of ground water?

options.text: Salty water is filtered while ground water is only sterilised
Ground water must be desalinated just like salty water
Both are treated in exactly the same way at the works
Salty water must have its dissolved salts removed

questions.explanation: Ground water needs filtering and sterilising; salty water needs dissolved salts removed as well.

questions.stem: Why is a life cycle assessment not a purely objective process?

options.text: Because different scientists measure the energy used in different units
Because the mass of waste made can never be measured accurately
Because a shortened LCA was used, so it is only slightly less precise
Allocating numerical values to pollutant effects requires value judgements

questions.explanation: This is the reason the specification gives for an LCA not being a purely objective process.

questions.stem: A council has data on four schemes. New raw material avoided each year: repair scheme 900 t, kerbside recycling 400 t, recycled bin bags 120 t, burning waste 0 t. Which scheme cuts the use of limited resources the most?

options.text: Kerbside recycling of bottles and cans
A repair scheme for household goods
Bin bags made from recycled waste
Burning waste to generate electricity

questions.explanation: The data gives the repair scheme 900 t, the largest saving of new raw material.

questions.stem: In Required practical 8, how is the mass of dissolved solids in a water sample found?

options.text: By measuring the pH of the water sample with a probe
By evaporating a set volume to dryness and weighing the residue
By weighing the distillate collected during distillation
By filtering the sample and weighing the filter paper

questions.explanation: The dissolved solids are left behind when the water evaporates, so the residue can be weighed.

questions.stem: Two teams carry out a full LCA on the same paint and reach opposite conclusions, although both used the same measured data for water, energy and waste. What is the best explanation?

options.text: One of the two teams must have made an arithmetic error somewhere
The teams gave the pollutant effects of this paint different weights
Pollutant effects cannot go into an LCA at all, so both teams guessed
Data on water and energy use is unreliable and varies by team

questions.explanation: Allocating values to pollutant effects requires value judgements, so the same data can support different conclusions.

questions.stem: A student distils a sample of sea water in Required practical 8. What is collected in the receiving tube?

options.text: Salt solution that is more concentrated than before
Sea water with all of its dissolved solids in it
Water that leaves no residue when it is evaporated
Water that must be pure because its pH is 7

questions.explanation: Only water evaporates and condenses, so the distillate is pure water and leaves no residue.
